class CalcCrackGrowth(PlotMixin):  # pragma: no cover
    """Crack growth object. This object is used to calculate the crack
    growth rate and the crack size. The class has been implemented
    using a Rust kernel to speed up the calculations.

    The crack size is numerically integrated over the crack growth
    curve. In this example we will consider the Paris' law, but the
    function can be used with any other crack growth curve.

    $$
    \\begin{cases}
        \\frac{da}{dN} & = C \\left( \\Delta K \\right)^{m} \\\\
        \\Delta K & = Y(a) \\cdot \\Delta \\sigma \\sqrt{\\pi a} \\\\
    \\end{cases}
    $$

    From the equations above, the crack growths rate can be expressed as a
    function of the stress range. Considering the Paris' law, as in this
    example, gives:

    $$
    \\frac{da}{dN} = C \\left( Y(a) \\cdot \\Delta \\sigma \\sqrt{\\pi a}
        \\right)^{m}
    $$

    se this crack growth rate together with the cycle step size to
    determine the incremental growth of the crack for this iteration:

    $$
    \\Delta a = \\frac{da}{dN} \\cdot \\Delta N
    $$

    The new crack size is then calculated by adding the incremental growth
    to the previous crack size:

    $$
    a_{j+1} = a_{j} + \\Delta a
    $$

    where $a_{j}$ is the crack size at the $j$-th cycle.

    The crack is grown iteratively either until the failure condition
    is met or until the stress history is over.

    If failure occurs, the total number of cycles that it took to grow the
    crack to the critical size becomes the predicted life of the part.


    Parameters
    ----------
    stress_range : np.ndarray
        Stress range array.
    count_cycle : np.ndarray
        Number of cycles array.
    slope : np.ndarray
        Slope array.
    intercept : np.ndarray
        Intercept array.
    threshold : float
        Threshold value.
    critical : float
        Critical value.
    crack_geometry : dict
        Crack geometry dictionary. It must contain the following keys:
        - "initial_depth": float
        - "_id": str



    Returns
    -------
    CalcCrackGrowth
        Crack growth object.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        stress_range: np.ndarray,
        count_cycle: np.ndarray,
        slope: np.ndarray,
        intercept: np.ndarray,
        threshold: float,
        critical: float,
        crack_type: str,
        crack_geometry: dict,
    ):

        assert intercept.size > 0 and intercept.size == slope.size
        assert np.min(stress_range) >= 0.0
        assert stress_range.size > 0 and stress_range.size == count_cycle.size
        self.stress_range = stress_range
        self.count_cycle = count_cycle
        self.slope = slope
        self.intercept = intercept
        self.threshold = threshold
        self.critical = critical
        self.crack_type = crack_type
        self.crack_geometry = crack_geometry
        cs, sif, factor, failure = self.calc_crack_depth()
        self.crack_depth = cs
        self.sif = sif
        self.geometry_factor = factor
        self.final_cycles = sum(self.count_cycle[: len(self.crack_depth)])
        self.failure = failure

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        """String representation of the object."""
        if getattr(self, "termination", None) == "geometry_limit":
            return "Crack growth object: geometry table limit reached."
        if self.failure:
            return "Crack growth object: to failure."
        return "Crack growth object: to maximum number of cycles - no failure."

    def plot(
        self, fig: Figure | None = None, ax: Axes | None = None
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Plot the crack depth recorded at the start of each legacy step.

        Depths use the same length unit as the supplied geometry.
        """
        fig, ax = make_axes(fig, ax)
        count = len(self.crack_depth)
        cycles = np.r_[0.0, np.cumsum(self.count_cycle[:count])][:count]
        ax.plot(cycles, self.crack_depth, marker="o" if count == 1 else None)
        ax.set(xlabel="Cycles at start of step", ylabel="Crack depth")
        ax.ticklabel_format(axis="y", useOffset=False)
        if not count:
            ax.set_title("No recorded crack depths")
        return fig, ax

    @property
    def size(self) -> int:
        """Size of the problem."""
        return self.stress_range.size

    @property
    def get_knees_sif(self) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""Get the SIF values at the knees of the Paris curve.

        For adjacent Paris branches with coefficients $C_i$ and exponents
        $m_i$, the stress intensity factor range at their intersection is

        $$
        \Delta K_i =
        \left(\frac{C_i}{C_{i+1}}\right)^{\frac{1}{m_{i+1} - m_i}}.
        $$
        """
        cg_crv_size = self.intercept.size
        knees_sif = np.empty(
            cg_crv_size - 1, dtype=np.float64
        )  # pylint: disable=E1133, C0301
        if cg_crv_size > 1:  # pylint: disable=E1133, C0301
            for i in range(cg_crv_size - 1):  # pylint: disable=E1133, C0301
                knees_sif[i] = (self.intercept[i] / self.intercept[i + 1]) ** (
                    1 / (self.slope[i + 1] - self.slope[i])
                )
        knees_sif = np.hstack(
            (
                np.array([0.9999999999 * self.threshold]),
                knees_sif,
                np.array([self.critical / 0.9999999999]),
            )
        )
        e_msg = (
            "Knee(s) not in between threshold and critical SIF."
            + "\nCheck the definitions of slope, intercept, "
            + "threshold, critical."
        )
        assert np.all(np.diff(knees_sif) > 0), e_msg
        return knees_sif

    def calc_growth_rate(
        self, stress_, crack_depth_
    ) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
        """Calculate the crack growth rate given the stress and the
        crack size using the Paris' law:

        $$
        \\frac{da}{dN} = \\text{intercept} \\, {\\Delta K)^{\\text{slope}}
        $$

        Parameters
        ----------
        stress_ : float
            Stress value.
        crack_depth_ : float
            Crack size value.

        Returns
        -------
        Tuple[float, float, float]
            Crack growth rate, stress intensity factor, and geometry factor.
        """

        sif, g_factor = get_sif(
            stress_, crack_depth_, self.crack_type, self.crack_geometry
        )
        knees = self.get_knees_sif
        if sif < self.threshold:
            the_growth_rate = 0.0
        elif sif >= self.critical:
            the_growth_rate = np.inf
        else:
            idx = np.digitize(np.asarray([sif]), knees, right=True) - 1
            the_growth_rate = self.intercept[idx][0] * sif ** self.slope[idx][0]

        return the_growth_rate, sif, g_factor

    def calc_crack_depth(
        self,
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, bool]:
        """Calculate the crack size and the SIF values.

        Using the assigned stress ranges and count-cycles arrays, the final
        crack size is calculated. The method iterates over the stress ranges
        and count-cycles arrays and updates the crack size at each step.

        ```python
        crack_depth = [crack_geometry["initial_depth"]]

        sifs = []
        factors = []
        for stress, count_cycle in zip(stress_range, count_cycle):
            for i in range(count_cycle):
                sifs.append(get_sif(stress,
                                    crack_depth, self.crack_geometry))
                factors.append(get_geometry_factor(crack_depth,
                                                   crack_type,
                                                   crack_geometry))
                if sifs[-1] >= critical:
                    return crack_depth, sifs, factors, True
                if sifs[-1] < threshold:
                    continue
                crack_depth.append(crack_depth[-1] +
                                   calc_growth_rate(stress, crack_depth))
        return crack_depth, sifs, factors, False
        ```

        Returns
        -------
        Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, bool]
            Crack size array, SIF array, geometric factor array, failure flag.
        """

        if self.crack_type not in ("HOL_CYL_01", "INF_SUR_00", "TABULATED"):
            raise NotImplementedError(
                "Geometric factor not implemented for assigned crack type."
            )
        dimensions = (
            cylinder_dimensions(self.crack_geometry)
            if self.crack_type == "HOL_CYL_01"
            else None
        )
        table = (
            (
                np.ascontiguousarray(
                    self.crack_geometry["depths"], dtype=float
                ),
                np.ascontiguousarray(
                    self.crack_geometry["factors"], dtype=float
                ),
            )
            if self.crack_type == "TABULATED"
            else None
        )
        crack_depth, sif, factor, self.termination, message = legacy_growth(
            (
                np.ascontiguousarray(self.stress_range, dtype=float),
                np.ascontiguousarray(self.count_cycle, dtype=float),
            ),
            (
                np.ascontiguousarray(self.slope, dtype=float),
                np.ascontiguousarray(self.intercept, dtype=float),
                np.ascontiguousarray(self.get_knees_sif[1:-1], dtype=float),
                (self.threshold, self.critical),
            ),
            self.crack_geometry["initial_depth"],
            dimensions,
            table,
        )
        print(message)
        failure = (
            self.termination != "geometry_limit"
            and len(crack_depth) < self.size
        )
        return crack_depth, sif, factor, failure

@pd.api.extensions.register_dataframe_accessor("cg")
class CrackGrowth:
    """Accessor for the crack growth calculation

    Parameters
    ----------
    pandas_obj : pd.DataFrame
        The pandas dataframe object that will be extended
        with the crack growth calculation results. The original dataframe must
        have the following columns:
        - stress_range
        - count_cycle
        - mean_stress
        The dataframe will be extended with the following columns:
        - crack_depth
        - sif
        - cumul_cycles
        - geometry_factor
    """

    def __init__(self, pandas_obj):
        # self._validate(pandas_obj)
        self._obj = pandas_obj
        self.cg_curve = pandas_obj.attrs.get("cg_curve")
        self.crack_geometry = pandas_obj.attrs.get("crack_geometry")
        self.final_cycles = pandas_obj.attrs.get("final_cycles")

    @staticmethod
    def _validate(obj):
        """Validate the input DataFrame. Raise an error if the input
        DataFrame does not contain the right columns.
        """
        if {
            "crack_depth",
        }.issubset(obj.columns):
            e_msg = "'crack_depth' already calculated"
            raise AttributeError(e_msg)

        if not {"count_cycle", "mean_stress", "stress_range"}.issubset(
            obj.columns
        ):
            e_msg = "Must have 'count_cycle', 'mean_stress' and 'stress_range'."
            raise AttributeError(e_msg)

    def calc_growth(
        self,
        cg_curve: ParisCurve,
        crack_geometry: AbstractCrackGeometry,
        express_mode: bool = False,
    ):
        """Calculate the crack_propagation of the given crack geometry.

        Parameters
        ----------
        cg_curve : py_fatigue.ParisCurve
            The crack growth curve
        crack_geometry : AbstractCrackGeometry
            The initial crack geometry
        express_mode : bool, optional
            If True, the crack propagation runs 'express', by default False

        Returns
        -------
        DataFrame
            The DataFrame with the results of the crack_growth analysis.
        """

        self._validate(self._obj)

        # Handle the stress ranges and cycle counts as they might be clustered
        # in a matrix and we need to iterate over single or "little" cycles
        # within the same stress range block

        if np.max(self._obj["count_cycle"]) > 1:
            if express_mode:
                splts = [
                    10 ** int(np.log10(cycle))
                    for cycle in self._obj["count_cycle"].values
                ]
            else:
                splts = [
                    int(cycle) for cycle in self._obj["count_cycle"].values
                ]
            splt_cyc = [
                split(int(cycle), n) if int(cycle) > 0 else [cycle]
                for cycle, n in zip(self._obj["count_cycle"].values, splts)
            ]
            splt_len = [len(_) for _ in splt_cyc]

            count_cycle = np.asarray(
                [float(item) for sublist in splt_cyc for item in sublist]
            )
            stress_range = np.repeat(self._obj["stress_range"].values, splt_len)
        else:
            stress_range = self._obj["stress_range"].values
            count_cycle = self._obj["count_cycle"].values

        # Handle the geometry
        crack_type = str(crack_geometry._id)
        if crack_type not in ("HOL_CYL_01", "INF_SUR_00", "TABULATED"):
            raise ValueError("Unsupported crack geometry")
        geometry = numeric_geometry(crack_geometry)  # type: ignore

        cg_ = CalcCrackGrowth(
            stress_range,
            count_cycle,
            cg_curve.slope,
            cg_curve.intercept,
            float(cg_curve.threshold),
            float(cg_curve.critical),
            crack_type,
            geometry,
        )

        self._obj.attrs["cg_curve"] = cg_curve
        self._obj.attrs["crack_geometry"] = crack_geometry
        self._obj.attrs["final_cycles"] = cg_.final_cycles
        self.cg_curve = cg_curve
        self.crack_geometry = crack_geometry
        self._obj.final_cycles = cg_.final_cycles
        self.final_cycles = cg_.final_cycles

        cumul_cycle = np.cumsum(cg_.count_cycle[: len(cg_.crack_depth)])
        # manage the fact that clustered cycles are split in cg analysys
        # while the df keeps them clustered
        d_l = len(self._obj) - len(cg_.crack_depth)
        if d_l >= 0:
            self._obj["crack_depth"] = np.concatenate(
                (cg_.crack_depth, np.full(d_l, np.nan))
            )
            self._obj["sif"] = np.concatenate((cg_.sif, np.full(d_l, np.nan)))
            self._obj["cumul_cycle"] = np.concatenate(
                (cumul_cycle, np.full(d_l, np.nan))
            )
            self._obj["geometry_factor"] = np.concatenate(
                (cg_.geometry_factor, np.full(d_l, np.nan))
            )
        else:
            # perform a piecewise cumsum, as the cycles are clustered
            # and the crack growth is performed on the split cycles

            # Convert indices to integers
            indices = [int(idx) for idx in indices]
            start_indices = [int(idx) for idx in start_indices]
            # fmt: off
            crack_depth = np.array([cg_.crack_depth[start:end].sum()
                                    for start, end in zip(start_indices,
                                                          indices)])

                            for start, end in zip(start_indices, indices)])
            cumul_cycle = np.array([cumul_cycle[start:end].sum()
                                    for start, end in zip(start_indices,
                                                          indices)])

                                        for start, end in zip(start_indices,
                                                              indices)])

            self._obj["geometry_factor"] = geometry_factor

Calculate the crack_propagation of the given crack geometry.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cg_curve ParisCurve

The crack growth curve

required crack_geometry AbstractCrackGeometry

The initial crack geometry

required express_mode bool

If True, the crack propagation runs 'express', by default False

Type Description DataFrame

The DataFrame with the results of the crack_growth analysis.

def calc_growth(
    self,
    cg_curve: ParisCurve,
    crack_geometry: AbstractCrackGeometry,
    express_mode: bool = False,
):
    """Calculate the crack_propagation of the given crack geometry.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cg_curve : py_fatigue.ParisCurve
        The crack growth curve
    crack_geometry : AbstractCrackGeometry
        The initial crack geometry
    express_mode : bool, optional
        If True, the crack propagation runs 'express', by default False

    Returns
    -------
    DataFrame
        The DataFrame with the results of the crack_growth analysis.
    """

    self._validate(self._obj)

    # Handle the stress ranges and cycle counts as they might be clustered
    # in a matrix and we need to iterate over single or "little" cycles
    # within the same stress range block

    if np.max(self._obj["count_cycle"]) > 1:
        if express_mode:
            splts = [
                10 ** int(np.log10(cycle))
                for cycle in self._obj["count_cycle"].values
            ]
        else:
            splts = [
                int(cycle) for cycle in self._obj["count_cycle"].values
            ]
        splt_cyc = [
            split(int(cycle), n) if int(cycle) > 0 else [cycle]
            for cycle, n in zip(self._obj["count_cycle"].values, splts)
        ]
        splt_len = [len(_) for _ in splt_cyc]

        count_cycle = np.asarray(
            [float(item) for sublist in splt_cyc for item in sublist]
        )
        stress_range = np.repeat(self._obj["stress_range"].values, splt_len)
    else:
        stress_range = self._obj["stress_range"].values
        count_cycle = self._obj["count_cycle"].values

    # Handle the geometry
    crack_type = str(crack_geometry._id)
    if crack_type not in ("HOL_CYL_01", "INF_SUR_00", "TABULATED"):
        raise ValueError("Unsupported crack geometry")
    geometry = numeric_geometry(crack_geometry)  # type: ignore

    cg_ = CalcCrackGrowth(
        stress_range,
        count_cycle,
        cg_curve.slope,
        cg_curve.intercept,
        float(cg_curve.threshold),
        float(cg_curve.critical),
        crack_type,
        geometry,
    )

    self._obj.attrs["cg_curve"] = cg_curve
    self._obj.attrs["crack_geometry"] = crack_geometry
    self._obj.attrs["final_cycles"] = cg_.final_cycles
    self.cg_curve = cg_curve
    self.crack_geometry = crack_geometry
    self._obj.final_cycles = cg_.final_cycles
    self.final_cycles = cg_.final_cycles

    cumul_cycle = np.cumsum(cg_.count_cycle[: len(cg_.crack_depth)])
    # manage the fact that clustered cycles are split in cg analysys
    # while the df keeps them clustered
    d_l = len(self._obj) - len(cg_.crack_depth)
    if d_l >= 0:
        self._obj["crack_depth"] = np.concatenate(
            (cg_.crack_depth, np.full(d_l, np.nan))
        )
        self._obj["sif"] = np.concatenate((cg_.sif, np.full(d_l, np.nan)))
        self._obj["cumul_cycle"] = np.concatenate(
            (cumul_cycle, np.full(d_l, np.nan))
        )
        self._obj["geometry_factor"] = np.concatenate(
            (cg_.geometry_factor, np.full(d_l, np.nan))
        )
    else:
        # perform a piecewise cumsum, as the cycles are clustered
        # and the crack growth is performed on the split cycles
        indices = np.cumsum(self._obj["count_cycle"].values).tolist()
        # Get the cumulative indices from count_cycles
        start_indices = [0] + indices[:-1]
        # Convert indices to integers
        indices = [int(idx) for idx in indices]
        start_indices = [int(idx) for idx in start_indices]
        # fmt: off
        crack_depth = np.array([cg_.crack_depth[start:end].sum()
                                for start, end in zip(start_indices,
                                                      indices)])
        sif = np.array([cg_.sif[start:end].sum()
                        for start, end in zip(start_indices, indices)])
        cumul_cycle = np.array([cumul_cycle[start:end].sum()
                                for start, end in zip(start_indices,
                                                      indices)])
        geometry_factor = np.array([cg_.geometry_factor[start:end].sum()
                                    for start, end in zip(start_indices,
                                                          indices)])
        # fmt: on
        self._obj["crack_depth"] = crack_depth
        self._obj["sif"] = sif
        self._obj["cumul_cycle"] = cumul_cycle
        self._obj["geometry_factor"] = geometry_factor
    self._obj.cg_curve = cg_curve
    self.cg_curve = cg_curve
    self._obj.crack_geometry = crack_geometry
    self.crack_geometry = crack_geometry
    return self._obj

get_crack_growth(
    cycle_count,
    cg_curve,
    crack_geometry,
    express_mode=False,

Calculate the crack size by numerically integrating the crack growth curve. In this example we will consider the Paris' law, but the function can be used with any other crack growth curve.

\[ \begin{cases} \frac{da}{dN} & = C \left( \Delta K \right)^{m} \\ \Delta K & = Y(a) \cdot \Delta \sigma \sqrt{\pi a} \\ \end{cases} \]

From the equations above, the crack growths rate can be expressed as a function of the stress range. Considering the Paris' law, as in this example, gives:

\[ \frac{da}{dN} = C \left( Y(a) \cdot \Delta \sigma \sqrt{\pi a} \right)^{m} \]

se this crack growth rate together with the cycle step size to determine the incremental growth of the crack for this iteration:

\[ \Delta a = \frac{da}{dN} \cdot \Delta N \]

The new crack size is then calculated by adding the incremental growth to the previous crack size:

\[ a_{j+1} = a_{j} + \Delta a \]

where \(a_{j}\) is the crack size at the \(j\)-th cycle.

The crack is grown iteratively either until the failure condition is met or until the stress history is over.

If failure occurs, the total number of cycles that it took to grow the crack to the critical size becomes the predicted life of the part.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cycle_count CycleCount

Cycle count object.

required cg_curve ParisCurve

The crack growth curve

required crack_geometry AbstractCrackGeometry

The initial crack geometry

required express_mode bool

If True, the crack growth is calculated using the express mode. This mode is faster but 'slightly' less accurate. The default is False.

False

Returns:

Type Description CalcCrackGrowth

The crack growth calculation object

Notes

Use matching stress units for the cycle count and the curve. For example, use MPa with MPa √mm and supply crack dimensions in mm. The solver uses the input values directly without converting units.

Source code in py_fatigue/damage/crack_growth.py 
def get_crack_growth(  # pragma: no cover
    cycle_count: CycleCount,
    cg_curve: ParisCurve,
    crack_geometry: AbstractCrackGeometry,
    express_mode: bool = False,
) -> CalcCrackGrowth:
    """Calculate the crack size by numerically integrating the crack growth
    curve. In this example we will consider the Paris' law, but the function
    can be used with any other crack growth curve.

    $$
    \\begin{cases}
        \\frac{da}{dN} & = C \\left( \\Delta K \\right)^{m} \\\\
        \\Delta K & = Y(a) \\cdot \\Delta \\sigma \\sqrt{\\pi a} \\\\
    \\end{cases}
    $$

    From the equations above, the crack growths rate can be expressed as a
    function of the stress range. Considering the Paris' law, as in this
    example, gives:

    $$
    \\frac{da}{dN} = C \\left( Y(a) \\cdot \\Delta \\sigma \\sqrt{\\pi a}
        \\right)^{m}
    $$

    se this crack growth rate together with the cycle step size to determine
    the incremental growth of the crack for this iteration:

    $$
    \\Delta a = \\frac{da}{dN} \\cdot \\Delta N
    $$

    The new crack size is then calculated by adding the incremental growth to
    the previous crack size:

    $$
    a_{j+1} = a_{j} + \\Delta a
    $$

    where $a_{j}$ is the crack size at the $j$-th cycle.

    The crack is grown iteratively either until the failure condition is met
    or until the stress history is over.

    If failure occurs, the total number of cycles that it took to grow the
    crack to the critical size becomes the predicted life of the part.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cycle_count : py_fatigue.CycleCount
        Cycle count object.
    cg_curve : py_fatigue.ParisCurve
        The crack growth curve
    crack_geometry : AbstractCrackGeometry
        The initial crack geometry
    express_mode : bool, optional
        If True, the crack growth is calculated using the express mode. This
        mode is faster but 'slightly' less accurate. The default is False.

    Returns
    -------
    CalcCrackGrowth
        The crack growth calculation object
    Notes
    -----
    Use matching stress units for the cycle count and the curve. For
    example, use MPa with MPa √mm and supply crack dimensions in mm.
    The solver uses the input values directly without converting units.
    """
    # Handle the stress ranges and cycle counts as they might be clustered
    # in a matrix and we need to iterate over single or "little" cycles
    # within the same stress range block
    intensity_unit = re.fullmatch(
        r"(Pa|kPa|MPa|GPa|psi|ksi)\s*(?:[·*]\s*)?"
        r"(?:√\s*(?:mm|cm|m|in)|sqrt\(\s*(?:mm|cm|m|in)\s*\))",
        cg_curve.unit.strip(),
    )
    if intensity_unit is None or cycle_count.unit.strip() != intensity_unit[1]:
        e_msg = (
            f"Cycle count unit ({cycle_count.unit}) and crack growth "
            f"curve unit ({cg_curve.unit}) are not compatible."
        )
        raise ValueError(e_msg)
    if np.max(cycle_count.count_cycle) > 1:
        if express_mode:
            splts = [
                10 ** int(np.log10(cycle)) for cycle in cycle_count.count_cycle
            ]
        else:
            splts = [int(cycle) for cycle in cycle_count.count_cycle]
        splt_cyc = [
            split(int(cycle), n) if int(cycle) > 0 else [cycle]
            for cycle, n in zip(cycle_count.count_cycle, splts)
        ]
        splt_len = [len(_) for _ in splt_cyc]

        count_cycle = np.asarray(
            [float(item) for sublist in splt_cyc for item in sublist]
        )
        stress_range = np.repeat(cycle_count.stress_range, splt_len)
    else:
        stress_range = cycle_count.stress_range
        count_cycle = cycle_count.count_cycle

    # Handle the geometry

    crack_type = str(crack_geometry._id)
    if crack_type not in ("HOL_CYL_01", "INF_SUR_00", "TABULATED"):
        raise ValueError("Unsupported crack geometry")
    geometry = numeric_geometry(crack_geometry)  # type: ignore
    cg = CalcCrackGrowth(
        stress_range,
        count_cycle,
        cg_curve.slope,
        cg_curve.intercept,
        float(cg_curve.threshold),
        float(cg_curve.critical),
        crack_type,
        geometry,
    )
    # crack_geometry.geometry_factor = cg.geometry_factor
    # crack_geometry.crack_depth_ = cg.crack_depth
    # crack_geometry.sif_ = cg.sif
    # crack_geometry.count_cycle_ = np.cumsum(
    #     cg.count_cycle[: len(cg.crack_depth)]
    # )
    # crack_geometry.final_cycles_ = cg.final_cycles
    return cg  # crack_geometry

def get_geometry_factor(  # pragma: no cover
    crack_depth: float,
    crack_type: str,
    crack_geometry: dict,  # pylint: disable=W0613, C0301
) -> float:
    """Get the geometric factor. This should be a function of the crack
    size. The default value is 1.0."""
    # Placeholder for future implementation
    if crack_type == "HOL_CYL_01":
        return f_hol_cyl_01(crack_depth, crack_geometry)
    if crack_type == "INF_SUR_00":
        return 1.0
    if crack_type == "TABULATED":
        depths = crack_geometry["depths"]
        if not depths[0] <= crack_depth <= depths[-1]:
            raise ValueError(
                "Crack depth is outside the geometry-factor table."
            )
        return float(np.interp(crack_depth, depths, crack_geometry["factors"]))

    e_msg = "Geometric factor not implemented for assigned crack type."
    raise NotImplementedError(e_msg)

def get_sif(  # pragma: no cover
    stress_: float,
    crack_depth_: float,
    crack_type: str,
    crack_geometry: dict,
) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Get the SIF value given the stress and the crack size. The
    method calculates the SIF value according to the following
    equation:

    $$
    SIF = Y(a) \\cdot \\Delta \\sigma \\cdot \\sqrt{\\pi a}
    $$

    Parameters
    ----------
    stress_ : float
        Stress value.
    crack_depth_ : float
        Crack size value.
    crack_type : str
        Crack type.
    crack_geometry : dict
        Crack geometry dictionary.

    Returns
    -------
    Tuple[float, float]
        SIF value, geometric factor.
    """
    y_1 = get_geometry_factor(crack_depth_, crack_type, crack_geometry)
    return stress_ * np.sqrt(np.pi * crack_depth_) * y_1, y_1

def numeric_geometry(
    geometry: AbstractCrackGeometry,
) -> dict[str, float | tuple[float, ...]]:
    """Return the geometry fields consumed by the crack-growth calculation."""
    fields = {
        key: value
        for key, value in vars(geometry).items()
        if isinstance(value, float)
    }
    if isinstance(geometry, TabulatedGeometryFactor):
        return {
            **fields,
            "depths": tuple(geometry.depths.tolist()),
            "factors": tuple(geometry.factors.tolist()),
        }
    return fields

Crack growth object. This object is used to calculate the crack growth rate and the crack size. The class has been implemented using a Rust kernel to speed up the calculations.

The crack size is numerically integrated over the crack growth curve. In this example we will consider the Paris' law, but the function can be used with any other crack growth curve.

\[ \begin{cases} \frac{da}{dN} & = C \left( \Delta K \right)^{m} \\ \Delta K & = Y(a) \cdot \Delta \sigma \sqrt{\pi a} \\ \end{cases} \]

From the equations above, the crack growths rate can be expressed as a function of the stress range. Considering the Paris' law, as in this example, gives:

\[ \frac{da}{dN} = C \left( Y(a) \cdot \Delta \sigma \sqrt{\pi a} \right)^{m} \]

se this crack growth rate together with the cycle step size to determine the incremental growth of the crack for this iteration:

\[ \Delta a = \frac{da}{dN} \cdot \Delta N \]

The new crack size is then calculated by adding the incremental growth to the previous crack size:

\[ a_{j+1} = a_{j} + \Delta a \]

where \(a_{j}\) is the crack size at the \(j\)-th cycle.

The crack is grown iteratively either until the failure condition is met or until the stress history is over.

If failure occurs, the total number of cycles that it took to grow the crack to the critical size becomes the predicted life of the part.

Intercept array.

class CalcCrackGrowth(PlotMixin):  # pragma: no cover
    """Crack growth object. This object is used to calculate the crack
    growth rate and the crack size. The class has been implemented
    using a Rust kernel to speed up the calculations.

    The crack size is numerically integrated over the crack growth
    curve. In this example we will consider the Paris' law, but the
    function can be used with any other crack growth curve.

    $$
    \\begin{cases}
        \\frac{da}{dN} & = C \\left( \\Delta K \\right)^{m} \\\\
        \\Delta K & = Y(a) \\cdot \\Delta \\sigma \\sqrt{\\pi a} \\\\
    \\end{cases}
    $$

    From the equations above, the crack growths rate can be expressed as a
    function of the stress range. Considering the Paris' law, as in this
    example, gives:

    $$
    \\frac{da}{dN} = C \\left( Y(a) \\cdot \\Delta \\sigma \\sqrt{\\pi a}
        \\right)^{m}
    $$

    se this crack growth rate together with the cycle step size to
    determine the incremental growth of the crack for this iteration:

    $$
    \\Delta a = \\frac{da}{dN} \\cdot \\Delta N
    $$

    The new crack size is then calculated by adding the incremental growth
    to the previous crack size:

    $$
    a_{j+1} = a_{j} + \\Delta a
    $$

    where $a_{j}$ is the crack size at the $j$-th cycle.

    The crack is grown iteratively either until the failure condition
    is met or until the stress history is over.

    If failure occurs, the total number of cycles that it took to grow the
    crack to the critical size becomes the predicted life of the part.


    Parameters
    ----------
    stress_range : np.ndarray
        Stress range array.
    count_cycle : np.ndarray
        Number of cycles array.
    slope : np.ndarray
        Slope array.
    intercept : np.ndarray
        Intercept array.
    threshold : float
        Threshold value.
    critical : float
        Critical value.
    crack_geometry : dict
        Crack geometry dictionary. It must contain the following keys:
        - "initial_depth": float
        - "_id": str



    Returns
    -------
    CalcCrackGrowth
        Crack growth object.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        stress_range: np.ndarray,
        count_cycle: np.ndarray,
        slope: np.ndarray,
        intercept: np.ndarray,
        threshold: float,
        critical: float,
        crack_type: str,
        crack_geometry: dict,
    ):

        assert intercept.size > 0 and intercept.size == slope.size
        assert np.min(stress_range) >= 0.0
        assert stress_range.size > 0 and stress_range.size == count_cycle.size
        self.stress_range = stress_range
        self.count_cycle = count_cycle
        self.slope = slope
        self.intercept = intercept
        self.threshold = threshold
        self.critical = critical
        self.crack_type = crack_type
        self.crack_geometry = crack_geometry
        cs, sif, factor, failure = self.calc_crack_depth()
        self.crack_depth = cs
        self.sif = sif
        self.geometry_factor = factor
        self.final_cycles = sum(self.count_cycle[: len(self.crack_depth)])
        self.failure = failure

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        """String representation of the object."""
        if getattr(self, "termination", None) == "geometry_limit":
            return "Crack growth object: geometry table limit reached."
        if self.failure:
            return "Crack growth object: to failure."
        return "Crack growth object: to maximum number of cycles - no failure."

    def plot(
        self, fig: Figure | None = None, ax: Axes | None = None
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Plot the crack depth recorded at the start of each legacy step.

        Depths use the same length unit as the supplied geometry.
        """
        fig, ax = make_axes(fig, ax)
        count = len(self.crack_depth)
        cycles = np.r_[0.0, np.cumsum(self.count_cycle[:count])][:count]
        ax.plot(cycles, self.crack_depth, marker="o" if count == 1 else None)
        ax.set(xlabel="Cycles at start of step", ylabel="Crack depth")
        ax.ticklabel_format(axis="y", useOffset=False)
        if not count:
            ax.set_title("No recorded crack depths")
        return fig, ax

    @property
    def size(self) -> int:
        """Size of the problem."""
        return self.stress_range.size

    @property
    def get_knees_sif(self) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""Get the SIF values at the knees of the Paris curve.

        For adjacent Paris branches with coefficients $C_i$ and exponents
        $m_i$, the stress intensity factor range at their intersection is

        $$
        \Delta K_i =
        \left(\frac{C_i}{C_{i+1}}\right)^{\frac{1}{m_{i+1} - m_i}}.
        $$
        """
        cg_crv_size = self.intercept.size
        knees_sif = np.empty(
            cg_crv_size - 1, dtype=np.float64
        )  # pylint: disable=E1133, C0301
        if cg_crv_size > 1:  # pylint: disable=E1133, C0301
            for i in range(cg_crv_size - 1):  # pylint: disable=E1133, C0301
                knees_sif[i] = (self.intercept[i] / self.intercept[i + 1]) ** (
                    1 / (self.slope[i + 1] - self.slope[i])
                )
        knees_sif = np.hstack(
            (
                np.array([0.9999999999 * self.threshold]),
                knees_sif,
                np.array([self.critical / 0.9999999999]),
            )
        )
        e_msg = (
            "Knee(s) not in between threshold and critical SIF."
            + "\nCheck the definitions of slope, intercept, "
            + "threshold, critical."
        )
        assert np.all(np.diff(knees_sif) > 0), e_msg
        return knees_sif

    def calc_growth_rate(
        self, stress_, crack_depth_
    ) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
        """Calculate the crack growth rate given the stress and the
        crack size using the Paris' law:

        $$
        \\frac{da}{dN} = \\text{intercept} \\, {\\Delta K)^{\\text{slope}}
        $$

        Parameters
        ----------
        stress_ : float
            Stress value.
        crack_depth_ : float
            Crack size value.

        Returns
        -------
        Tuple[float, float, float]
            Crack growth rate, stress intensity factor, and geometry factor.
        """

        sif, g_factor = get_sif(
            stress_, crack_depth_, self.crack_type, self.crack_geometry
        )
        knees = self.get_knees_sif
        if sif < self.threshold:
            the_growth_rate = 0.0
        elif sif >= self.critical:
            the_growth_rate = np.inf
        else:
            idx = np.digitize(np.asarray([sif]), knees, right=True) - 1
            the_growth_rate = self.intercept[idx][0] * sif ** self.slope[idx][0]

        return the_growth_rate, sif, g_factor

    def calc_crack_depth(
        self,
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, bool]:
        """Calculate the crack size and the SIF values.

        Using the assigned stress ranges and count-cycles arrays, the final
        crack size is calculated. The method iterates over the stress ranges
        and count-cycles arrays and updates the crack size at each step.

        ```python
        crack_depth = [crack_geometry["initial_depth"]]

        sifs = []
        factors = []
        for stress, count_cycle in zip(stress_range, count_cycle):
            for i in range(count_cycle):
                sifs.append(get_sif(stress,
                                    crack_depth, self.crack_geometry))
                factors.append(get_geometry_factor(crack_depth,
                                                   crack_type,
                                                   crack_geometry))
                if sifs[-1] >= critical:
                    return crack_depth, sifs, factors, True
                if sifs[-1] < threshold:
                    continue
                crack_depth.append(crack_depth[-1] +
                                   calc_growth_rate(stress, crack_depth))
        return crack_depth, sifs, factors, False
        ```

        Returns
        -------
        Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, bool]
            Crack size array, SIF array, geometric factor array, failure flag.
        """

        if self.crack_type not in ("HOL_CYL_01", "INF_SUR_00", "TABULATED"):
            raise NotImplementedError(
                "Geometric factor not implemented for assigned crack type."
            )
        dimensions = (
            cylinder_dimensions(self.crack_geometry)
            if self.crack_type == "HOL_CYL_01"
            else None
        )
        table = (
            (
                np.ascontiguousarray(
                    self.crack_geometry["depths"], dtype=float
                ),
                np.ascontiguousarray(
                    self.crack_geometry["factors"], dtype=float
                ),
            )
            if self.crack_type == "TABULATED"
            else None
        )
        crack_depth, sif, factor, self.termination, message = legacy_growth(
            (
                np.ascontiguousarray(self.stress_range, dtype=float),
                np.ascontiguousarray(self.count_cycle, dtype=float),
            ),
            (
                np.ascontiguousarray(self.slope, dtype=float),
                np.ascontiguousarray(self.intercept, dtype=float),
                np.ascontiguousarray(self.get_knees_sif[1:-1], dtype=float),
                (self.threshold, self.critical),
            ),
            self.crack_geometry["initial_depth"],
            dimensions,
            table,
        )
        print(message)
        failure = (
            self.termination != "geometry_limit"
            and len(crack_depth) < self.size
        )
        return crack_depth, sif, factor, failure

def calc_growth_rate(
    self, stress_, crack_depth_
) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Calculate the crack growth rate given the stress and the
    crack size using the Paris' law:

    $$
    \\frac{da}{dN} = \\text{intercept} \\, {\\Delta K)^{\\text{slope}}
    $$

    Parameters
    ----------
    stress_ : float
        Stress value.
    crack_depth_ : float
        Crack size value.

    Returns
    -------
    Tuple[float, float, float]
        Crack growth rate, stress intensity factor, and geometry factor.
    """

    sif, g_factor = get_sif(
        stress_, crack_depth_, self.crack_type, self.crack_geometry
    )
    knees = self.get_knees_sif
    if sif < self.threshold:
        the_growth_rate = 0.0
    elif sif >= self.critical:
        the_growth_rate = np.inf
    else:
        idx = np.digitize(np.asarray([sif]), knees, right=True) - 1
        the_growth_rate = self.intercept[idx][0] * sif ** self.slope[idx][0]

    return the_growth_rate, sif, g_factor

def plot(
    self, fig: Figure | None = None, ax: Axes | None = None
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
    """Plot the crack depth recorded at the start of each legacy step.

    Depths use the same length unit as the supplied geometry.
    """
    fig, ax = make_axes(fig, ax)
    count = len(self.crack_depth)
    cycles = np.r_[0.0, np.cumsum(self.count_cycle[:count])][:count]
    ax.plot(cycles, self.crack_depth, marker="o" if count == 1 else None)
    ax.set(xlabel="Cycles at start of step", ylabel="Crack depth")
    ax.ticklabel_format(axis="y", useOffset=False)
    if not count:
        ax.set_title("No recorded crack depths")
    return fig, ax

class CenterThroughCrack(_PlateCrack):
    """TC01 center crack with plate and crack half-widths in mm."""

    half_width: float
    half_length: float

    def stress_intensity(self, stress: float) -> float:
        """Evaluate opening-mode intensity in MPa sqrt(mm)."""
        section, sizes, _ = _plate_state(self)
        factor, _ = plate_factors(section, sizes)
        return stress * factor

    def plot(
        self,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        *,
        result: GrowthResult | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Draw the crack and optionally overlay its last accepted profile."""
        final = _final_profile((self.half_length,), result)
        end = ([-final[0], final[0]], [0, 0]) if final is not None else None
        fig, ax = make_axes(fig, ax)
        ax.plot(
            [-self.half_width, self.half_width], [0, 0], label="Plate width"
        )
        _plot_profiles(
            ax, ([-self.half_length, self.half_length], [0, 0]), end, "Crack"
        )
        ax.set(
            xlabel="Position across plate (mm)", title="Center through crack"
        )
        ax.yaxis.set_visible(False)
        ax.legend()
        return fig, ax

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CircumferentialCylinderSurfaceCrack(PlotMixin):
    """External SC05 thumbnail crack subject to remote axial tension.

    Parameters
    ----------
    inner_radius, thickness : float
        Pipe inner radius and wall thickness in mm.
    depth, half_length : float
        Radial depth and outer-surface arc half-length in mm.

    Notes
    -----
    Interpolates NASA TM-87594 Table 1 within 1 <= R/t <= 10,
    0.2 <= a/t <= 0.8 and 0.6 <= a/c <= 1. The crack is external.
    """

    inner_radius: float
    thickness: float
    depth: float
    half_length: float

    def stress_intensity(self, stress: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
        """Return deepest and free-surface K in MPa sqrt(mm)."""
        section, sizes, _ = _plate_state(self)
        depth, surface = plate_factors(section, sizes)
        return stress * depth, stress * surface

    def plot(
        self,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        *,
        result: GrowthResult | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Draw the pipe section and the initial and last accepted fronts."""
        self.stress_intensity(1.0)
        final = _final_profile((self.depth, self.half_length), result)
        fig, ax = make_axes(fig, ax)
        radius = self.inner_radius + self.thickness
        angle = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 201)
        for wall, label in (
            (radius, "Outer wall"),
            (self.inner_radius, "Inner wall"),
        ):
            ax.plot(wall * np.cos(angle), wall * np.sin(angle), label=label)
        _plot_profiles(
            ax,
            _curved_surface_front(radius, self.depth, self.half_length),
            _curved_surface_front(radius, *final) if final else None,
            "Crack front",
        )
        ax.set(
            xlabel="Section x (mm)",
            ylabel="Section y (mm)",
            title="SC05 · External circumferential pipe crack",
            aspect="equal",
        )
        ax.legend()
        return fig, ax

@pd.api.extensions.register_dataframe_accessor("cg")
class CrackGrowth:
    """Accessor for the crack growth calculation

    Parameters
    ----------
    pandas_obj : pd.DataFrame
        The pandas dataframe object that will be extended
        with the crack growth calculation results. The original dataframe must
        have the following columns:
        - stress_range
        - count_cycle
        - mean_stress
        The dataframe will be extended with the following columns:
        - crack_depth
        - sif
        - cumul_cycles
        - geometry_factor
    """

    def __init__(self, pandas_obj):
        # self._validate(pandas_obj)
        self._obj = pandas_obj
        self.cg_curve = pandas_obj.attrs.get("cg_curve")
        self.crack_geometry = pandas_obj.attrs.get("crack_geometry")
        self.final_cycles = pandas_obj.attrs.get("final_cycles")

    @staticmethod
    def _validate(obj):
        """Validate the input DataFrame. Raise an error if the input
        DataFrame does not contain the right columns.
        """
        if {
            "crack_depth",
        }.issubset(obj.columns):
            e_msg = "'crack_depth' already calculated"
            raise AttributeError(e_msg)

        if not {"count_cycle", "mean_stress", "stress_range"}.issubset(
            obj.columns
        ):
            e_msg = "Must have 'count_cycle', 'mean_stress' and 'stress_range'."
            raise AttributeError(e_msg)

    def calc_growth(
        self,
        cg_curve: ParisCurve,
        crack_geometry: AbstractCrackGeometry,
        express_mode: bool = False,
    ):
        """Calculate the crack_propagation of the given crack geometry.

        Parameters
        ----------
        cg_curve : py_fatigue.ParisCurve
            The crack growth curve
        crack_geometry : AbstractCrackGeometry
            The initial crack geometry
        express_mode : bool, optional
            If True, the crack propagation runs 'express', by default False

        Returns
        -------
        DataFrame
            The DataFrame with the results of the crack_growth analysis.
        """

        self._validate(self._obj)

        # Handle the stress ranges and cycle counts as they might be clustered
        # in a matrix and we need to iterate over single or "little" cycles
        # within the same stress range block

        if np.max(self._obj["count_cycle"]) > 1:
            if express_mode:
                splts = [
                    10 ** int(np.log10(cycle))
                    for cycle in self._obj["count_cycle"].values
                ]
            else:
                splts = [
                    int(cycle) for cycle in self._obj["count_cycle"].values
                ]
            splt_cyc = [
                split(int(cycle), n) if int(cycle) > 0 else [cycle]
                for cycle, n in zip(self._obj["count_cycle"].values, splts)
            ]
            splt_len = [len(_) for _ in splt_cyc]

            count_cycle = np.asarray(
                [float(item) for sublist in splt_cyc for item in sublist]
            )
            stress_range = np.repeat(self._obj["stress_range"].values, splt_len)
        else:
            stress_range = self._obj["stress_range"].values
            count_cycle = self._obj["count_cycle"].values

        # Handle the geometry
        crack_type = str(crack_geometry._id)
        if crack_type not in ("HOL_CYL_01", "INF_SUR_00", "TABULATED"):
            raise ValueError("Unsupported crack geometry")
        geometry = numeric_geometry(crack_geometry)  # type: ignore

        cg_ = CalcCrackGrowth(
            stress_range,
            count_cycle,
            cg_curve.slope,
            cg_curve.intercept,
            float(cg_curve.threshold),
            float(cg_curve.critical),
            crack_type,
            geometry,
        )

        self._obj.attrs["cg_curve"] = cg_curve
        self._obj.attrs["crack_geometry"] = crack_geometry
        self._obj.attrs["final_cycles"] = cg_.final_cycles
        self.cg_curve = cg_curve
        self.crack_geometry = crack_geometry
        self._obj.final_cycles = cg_.final_cycles
        self.final_cycles = cg_.final_cycles

        cumul_cycle = np.cumsum(cg_.count_cycle[: len(cg_.crack_depth)])
        # manage the fact that clustered cycles are split in cg analysys
        # while the df keeps them clustered
        d_l = len(self._obj) - len(cg_.crack_depth)
        if d_l >= 0:
            self._obj["crack_depth"] = np.concatenate(
                (cg_.crack_depth, np.full(d_l, np.nan))
            )
            self._obj["sif"] = np.concatenate((cg_.sif, np.full(d_l, np.nan)))
            self._obj["cumul_cycle"] = np.concatenate(
                (cumul_cycle, np.full(d_l, np.nan))
            )
            self._obj["geometry_factor"] = np.concatenate(
                (cg_.geometry_factor, np.full(d_l, np.nan))
            )
        else:
            # perform a piecewise cumsum, as the cycles are clustered
            # and the crack growth is performed on the split cycles
            indices = np.cumsum(self._obj["count_cycle"].values).tolist()
            # Get the cumulative indices from count_cycles
            start_indices = [0] + indices[:-1]
            # Convert indices to integers
            indices = [int(idx) for idx in indices]
            start_indices = [int(idx) for idx in start_indices]
            # fmt: off
            crack_depth = np.array([cg_.crack_depth[start:end].sum()
                                    for start, end in zip(start_indices,
                                                          indices)])
            sif = np.array([cg_.sif[start:end].sum()
                            for start, end in zip(start_indices, indices)])
            cumul_cycle = np.array([cumul_cycle[start:end].sum()
                                    for start, end in zip(start_indices,
                                                          indices)])
            geometry_factor = np.array([cg_.geometry_factor[start:end].sum()
                                        for start, end in zip(start_indices,
                                                              indices)])
            # fmt: on
            self._obj["crack_depth"] = crack_depth
            self._obj["sif"] = sif
            self._obj["cumul_cycle"] = cumul_cycle
            self._obj["geometry_factor"] = geometry_factor
        self._obj.cg_curve = cg_curve
        self.cg_curve = cg_curve
        self._obj.crack_geometry = crack_geometry
        self.crack_geometry = crack_geometry
        return self._obj

        If True, the crack propagation runs 'express', by default False

    -------
    DataFrame
        The DataFrame with the results of the crack_growth analysis.
    """

    self._validate(self._obj)

    # Handle the stress ranges and cycle counts as they might be clustered
    # in a matrix and we need to iterate over single or "little" cycles
    # within the same stress range block

    if np.max(self._obj["count_cycle"]) > 1:
        if express_mode:
            splts = [
                10 ** int(np.log10(cycle))
                for cycle in self._obj["count_cycle"].values
            ]
        else:
            splts = [
                int(cycle) for cycle in self._obj["count_cycle"].values
            ]
        splt_cyc = [
            split(int(cycle), n) if int(cycle) > 0 else [cycle]
            for cycle, n in zip(self._obj["count_cycle"].values, splts)
        ]
        splt_len = [len(_) for _ in splt_cyc]

        count_cycle = np.asarray(
            [float(item) for sublist in splt_cyc for item in sublist]
        )
        stress_range = np.repeat(self._obj["stress_range"].values, splt_len)
    else:
        stress_range = self._obj["stress_range"].values
        count_cycle = self._obj["count_cycle"].values

    # Handle the geometry
    crack_type = str(crack_geometry._id)
    if crack_type not in ("HOL_CYL_01", "INF_SUR_00", "TABULATED"):
        raise ValueError("Unsupported crack geometry")
    geometry = numeric_geometry(crack_geometry)  # type: ignore

    cg_ = CalcCrackGrowth(
        stress_range,
        count_cycle,
        cg_curve.slope,
        cg_curve.intercept,
        float(cg_curve.threshold),
        float(cg_curve.critical),
        crack_type,
        geometry,
    )

    self._obj.attrs["cg_curve"] = cg_curve
    self._obj.attrs["crack_geometry"] = crack_geometry
    self._obj.attrs["final_cycles"] = cg_.final_cycles
    self.cg_curve = cg_curve
    self.crack_geometry = crack_geometry
    self._obj.final_cycles = cg_.final_cycles
    self.final_cycles = cg_.final_cycles

    cumul_cycle = np.cumsum(cg_.count_cycle[: len(cg_.crack_depth)])
    # manage the fact that clustered cycles are split in cg analysys
    # while the df keeps them clustered
    d_l = len(self._obj) - len(cg_.crack_depth)
    if d_l >= 0:
        self._obj["crack_depth"] = np.concatenate(
            (cg_.crack_depth, np.full(d_l, np.nan))
        )
        self._obj["sif"] = np.concatenate((cg_.sif, np.full(d_l, np.nan)))
        self._obj["cumul_cycle"] = np.concatenate(
            (cumul_cycle, np.full(d_l, np.nan))
        )
        self._obj["geometry_factor"] = np.concatenate(
            (cg_.geometry_factor, np.full(d_l, np.nan))
        )
    else:
        # perform a piecewise cumsum, as the cycles are clustered
        # and the crack growth is performed on the split cycles
        indices = np.cumsum(self._obj["count_cycle"].values).tolist()
        # Get the cumulative indices from count_cycles
        start_indices = [0] + indices[:-1]
        # Convert indices to integers
        indices = [int(idx) for idx in indices]
        start_indices = [int(idx) for idx in start_indices]
        # fmt: off
        crack_depth = np.array([cg_.crack_depth[start:end].sum()
                                for start, end in zip(start_indices,
                                                      indices)])
        sif = np.array([cg_.sif[start:end].sum()
                        for start, end in zip(start_indices, indices)])
        cumul_cycle = np.array([cumul_cycle[start:end].sum()
                                for start, end in zip(start_indices,
                                                      indices)])
        geometry_factor = np.array([cg_.geometry_factor[start:end].sum()
                                    for start, end in zip(start_indices,
                                                          indices)])
        # fmt: on
        self._obj["crack_depth"] = crack_depth
        self._obj["sif"] = sif
        self._obj["cumul_cycle"] = cumul_cycle
        self._obj["geometry_factor"] = geometry_factor
    self._obj.cg_curve = cg_curve
    self.cg_curve = cg_curve
    self._obj.crack_geometry = crack_geometry
    self.crack_geometry = crack_geometry
    return self._obj

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EdgeThroughCrack(_PlateCrack):
    """TC02 single edge crack under remote tension with dimensions in mm.

    Supply the full plate width and the crack length measured from one
    edge. The tension solution is supported through a length/width of 0.8.
    """

    width: float
    length: float

    def stress_intensity(self, stress: float) -> float:
        """Evaluate opening-mode intensity in MPa sqrt(mm)."""
        section, sizes, _ = _plate_state(self)
        factor, _ = plate_factors(section, sizes)
        return stress * factor

    def plot(
        self,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        *,
        result: GrowthResult | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Draw the crack and optionally overlay its last accepted profile."""
        final = _final_profile((self.length,), result)
        end = ([0, final[0]], [0, 0]) if final is not None else None
        fig, ax = make_axes(fig, ax)
        ax.plot([0, self.width], [0, 0], label="Plate width")
        _plot_profiles(ax, ([0, self.length], [0, 0]), end, "Crack")
        ax.set(xlabel="Position across plate (mm)", title="Edge through crack")
        ax.yaxis.set_visible(False)
        ax.legend()
        return fig, ax

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GrowthResult(PlotMixin):
    """Accepted points and the reason propagation ended."""

    history: tuple[GrowthPoint, ...]
    termination: str
    dimension_names: tuple[str, ...] = field(
        default=(), compare=False, repr=False
    )

    @property
    def final_cycles(self) -> float:
        """Return the cycle count of the last accepted state, or zero."""
        return self.history[-1].cycles if self.history else 0.0

    def plot(
        self,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        *,
        label: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Plot the accepted crack dimensions against cumulative cycles.

        Use `label` as a legend prefix when overlaying several simulations.
        """
        fig, ax = make_axes(fig, ax)
        ax.set(xlabel="Cycles", ylabel="Crack dimension (mm)")
        if not self.history:
            if not ax.has_data():
                ax.set_title("No accepted crack states")
            return fig, ax

        dimensions = self.dimension_names or (
            ("Half-length",)
            if len(self.history[0].sizes) == 1
            else ("Depth", "Half-length")
        )
        cycles = [point.cycles for point in self.history]
        for index, name in enumerate(dimensions):
            ax.plot(
                cycles,
                [point.sizes[index] for point in self.history],
                marker="o" if len(cycles) == 1 else None,
                label=f"{label} · {name}" if label else name,
            )
        ax.legend()
        return fig, ax

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HoleBoreSurfaceCrack(PlotMixin):
    """SC11 bore crack at a centered circular hole under remote tension.

    Parameters
    ----------
    width, thickness, hole_diameter : float
        Full plate width and thickness and the hole diameter in mm.
    depth, half_length : float
        Radial depth into the ligament and half-length along the bore in
        mm. These are c and a, respectively, in NASA TM-85793.
    crack_count : int
        One crack, or two identical cracks on opposite sides of the bore.
        Each starts halfway through the plate.

    Notes
    -----
    NASA TM-85793 requires 0.2 <= a/c <= 2, a < t/2, 0.5 <= D/t <= 2,
    and (D + 2c)/W < 0.5, where t and W below denote full plate dimensions.
    """

    width: float
    thickness: float
    hole_diameter: float
    depth: float
    half_length: float
    crack_count: int

    def stress_intensity(self, stress: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
        """Return radial-tip and bore-tip K in MPa sqrt(mm)."""
        section, sizes, _ = _plate_state(self)
        radial, bore = plate_factors(section, sizes)
        return stress * radial, stress * bore

    def plot(
        self,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        *,
        result: GrowthResult | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Draw the plate section and the initial and last accepted fronts."""
        self.stress_intensity(1.0)
        final = _final_profile((self.depth, self.half_length), result)
        fig, ax = make_axes(fig, ax)
        radius, width, height = (
            self.hole_diameter / 2,
            self.width / 2,
            self.thickness / 2,
        )
        for side, label in ((-1, "Left ligament"), (1, "Right ligament")):
            ax.plot(
                [
                    side * radius,
                    side * width,
                    side * width,
                    side * radius,
                    side * radius,
                ],
                [-height, -height, height, height, -height],
                label=label,
            )
        angle = np.linspace(-np.pi / 2, np.pi / 2, 101)
        cosine, sine = np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle)
        cosine[[0, -1]] = 0.0

        def fronts(depth: float, span: float) -> tuple[ArrayLike, ArrayLike]:
            radial = radius + depth * cosine
            bore = span * sine
            if self.crack_count == 2:
                return np.r_[radial, np.nan, -radial], np.r_[bore, np.nan, bore]
            return radial, bore

        _plot_profiles(
            ax,
            fronts(self.depth, self.half_length),
            fronts(*final) if final else None,
            "Crack front",
        )
        ax.set(
            xlabel="Position across plate (mm)",
            ylabel="Position along bore (mm)",
            title=f"SC11 · Plate hole ({self.crack_count} crack(s))",
            aspect="equal",
        )
        ax.legend()
        return fig, ax

@dataclass(repr=False)
class HollowCylinder(AbstractCrackGeometry):
    """Class to initalise and store the crack geometry data on a
    hollow cylindrical section.

    The crack is assumed to maintain its width to depth ratio.

    >>> # Example drawing of a hollow cylinder with external crack
    >>> #        ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
    >>> #        │              ▄▄▄▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▚▄▄▖            │
    >>> #        │          ▗▄▀▀             ▝▀▚▄         │
    >>> #        │        ▄▀▘                    ▀▖       │
    >>> #        │       ▞    crack front         ▝▀▖     │
    >>> #        │     ▗▀     │      ▄▄▄▖           ▝▖    │
    >>> #        │    ▗███▄▖<─┘  ▗▟▀▀   ▀▀▚▖         ▐    │
    >>> #        │    ▟█████▖   ▟▘         ▀▙         ▌   │
    >>> #        │2c─>███████   ▌       r_i ▐         ▐   │
    >>> #        │    ███████   ▌     ↑<───>▐         ▐   │
    >>> #        │    ▜█████▘   ▜▖    │    ▄▛         ▌   │
    >>> #        │   │▝███▀▘│    ▝▜▄▄ │ ▄▄▞▘         ▐    │
    >>> #        │   │ ▝▄   │        ▀│▀▘           ▗▘    │
    >>> #        │   │   ▚  │      r_o│           ▗▄▘     │
    >>> #        │   │    ▚▄│         │          ▗▘       │
    >>> #        │   │   a  ▀▚▄▖      ↓       ▄▞▀▘        │
    >>> #        │   │<────>│  ▝▀▀▚▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▀▀▀            │
    >>> #        └────────────────────────────────────────┘
    >>> #

    Attributes
    ----------
    initial_depth : float
        The initial depth of the crack.
    outer_diameter : float
        The outer diameter of the part.
    thickness : float
        The thickness of the part.
    height : float
        The height of the part.
    crack_position : float
        The position of the crack on the part.
    width_to_depth_ratio : float
        The ratio of the width to the depth of the crack.
    """

    outer_diameter: PositiveFloat
    thickness: PositiveFloat
    height: PositiveFloat
    crack_position: str
    width_to_depth_ratio: PositiveFloat = 2.0

    _id = property(
        lambda self: (
            "HOL_CYL_00" if self.crack_position == "internal" else "HOL_CYL_01"
        )
    )

    @validator("thickness")
    @classmethod
    def thickness_validator(
        cls, v: PositiveFloat, values: dict
    ) -> PositiveFloat:
        """Validate the thickness of the part."""
        if v >= values["outer_diameter"] / 2:
            e_msg = "thickness is greater than or equal to the outer radius"
            raise ValueError(e_msg)
        if v <= values["initial_depth"]:
            e_msg = "thickness is less than or equal to the initial depth"
            raise ValueError(e_msg)
        return v

    @validator("crack_position")
    @classmethod
    def crack_position_validator(cls, v: str) -> str:
        """Validate the crack position string."""
        if v not in ["internal", "external"]:
            raise ValueError(
                "crack position must be either 'internal' or 'external'"
            )
        return v

    @property
    def geometry_factor(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Get the geometric factor. This should be a function of the crack
        size. The default value is 1.0."""
        return np.empty(0)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return (
            super().__str__()[:-3]
            + f",\n  outer_diameter={self.outer_diameter}"
            + f",\n  thickness={self.thickness}"
            + f",\n  height={self.height}"
            + f",\n  width_to_depth_ratio={self.width_to_depth_ratio}"
            + f",\n  crack_position={self.crack_position},\n)"
        )

    def plot(
        self,
        fig: Optional[matplotlib.figure.Figure] = None,
        ax: Optional[matplotlib.axes.Axes] = None,
        **kwargs: dict,
    ) -> tuple:  # pragma: no cover
        """Draw the hollow cylinder cross-section and crack.

        For an internal crack, the line indicates depth from the inner wall.

        Parameters
        ----------
        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure, optional
            The figure to plot on.
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            The axis to plot on.
        **kwargs : dict
            Keyword arguments to pass to the matplotlib plot function.

        Returns
        -------
        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
            The figure that was plotted on.
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes
        """

        if self.crack_position == "external":
            return self._plot_external_crack(fig=fig, ax=ax, **kwargs)

        fig, axes = pfu.make_axes(fig, ax)
        outer_radius = self.outer_diameter / 2
        inner_radius = outer_radius - self.thickness
        radii = (outer_radius, inner_radius)
        angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 101)
        for radius in radii:
            axes.plot(radius * np.cos(angles), radius * np.sin(angles), c="k")
        axes.plot(
            [inner_radius, inner_radius + self.initial_depth],
            [0, 0],
            c="firebrick",
            label="Internal crack depth",
            **kwargs,
        )
        axes.set(aspect="equal", title="Hollow cylinder cross-section")
        axes.legend()
        return fig, axes

    def _plot_external_crack(
        self,
        depth: Optional[PositiveFloat] = None,
        fig: Optional[matplotlib.figure.Figure] = None,
        ax: Optional[matplotlib.axes.Axes] = None,
        **kwargs: dict,
    ) -> tuple:  # pragma: no cover
        """Plot the crack front when the crack is located on the external
        surface of the hollow cylinder.

        Parameters
        ----------
        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure, optional
            The figure to plot on.
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            The axis to plot on.
        **kwargs : dict
            Keyword arguments to pass to the matplotlib plot function.

        Returns
        -------
        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
            The figure that was plotted on.
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes
        """
        if depth is None:
            depth = self.initial_depth
        angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 100)
        r_o = self.outer_diameter / 2
        r_i = r_o - self.thickness

        x_o = r_o * np.cos(angles)
        y_o = r_o * np.sin(angles)
        x_i = r_i * np.cos(angles)
        y_i = r_i * np.sin(angles)

        crack_width = self.width_to_depth_ratio * depth
        c_angle = crack_width / r_o  # crack angle
        c_v = r_o * np.sin(c_angle)
        a_h = depth - r_o * (1 - np.cos(c_angle))
        r_e = (c_v**2 + a_h**2) / (2 * a_h)  # radius of crack-front arc
        # angle of crack-front arc
        beta = np.arcsin(c_v / r_e)
        theta = np.linspace(-beta, beta, 100)  # θ (crack-front angle)
        phi = np.linspace(np.pi - c_angle, np.pi + c_angle, 100)

        # crack-front arc
        x_c = r_e * np.cos(theta) - (r_o + r_e - depth)
        y_c = r_e * np.sin(theta)
        x_c = np.append(x_c, r_o * np.cos(phi))
        y_c = np.append(y_c, r_o * np.sin(phi))

        # plot
        fig, axes = pfu.make_axes(fig=fig, ax=ax)
        axes.set_aspect("equal")
        axes.plot(x_o, y_o, c="k", lw=0.5, **kwargs)  # type: ignore

def plot(
    self,
    fig: Optional[matplotlib.figure.Figure] = None,
    ax: Optional[matplotlib.axes.Axes] = None,
    **kwargs: dict,
) -> tuple:  # pragma: no cover
    """Draw the hollow cylinder cross-section and crack.

    For an internal crack, the line indicates depth from the inner wall.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure, optional
        The figure to plot on.
    ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
        The axis to plot on.
    **kwargs : dict
        Keyword arguments to pass to the matplotlib plot function.

    Returns
    -------
    fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
        The figure that was plotted on.
    ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes
    """

    if self.crack_position == "external":
        return self._plot_external_crack(fig=fig, ax=ax, **kwargs)

    fig, axes = pfu.make_axes(fig, ax)
    outer_radius = self.outer_diameter / 2
    inner_radius = outer_radius - self.thickness
    radii = (outer_radius, inner_radius)
    angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 101)
    for radius in radii:
        axes.plot(radius * np.cos(angles), radius * np.sin(angles), c="k")
    axes.plot(
        [inner_radius, inner_radius + self.initial_depth],
        [0, 0],
        c="firebrick",
        label="Internal crack depth",
        **kwargs,
    )
    axes.set(aspect="equal", title="Hollow cylinder cross-section")
    axes.legend()
    return fig, axes

@validator("thickness")
@classmethod
def thickness_validator(
    cls, v: PositiveFloat, values: dict
) -> PositiveFloat:
    """Validate the thickness of the part."""
    if v >= values["outer_diameter"] / 2:
        e_msg = "thickness is greater than or equal to the outer radius"
        raise ValueError(e_msg)
    if v <= values["initial_depth"]:
        e_msg = "thickness is less than or equal to the initial depth"
        raise ValueError(e_msg)
    return v

Supply the calibrated C and n, threshold and toughness exponents p and q, long-crack threshold at R=0, threshold fanning constant, fixed toughness, Newman constraint factor and fitted maximum-to-flow stress ratio. Use MPa sqrt(mm) for stress intensity parameters and mm/cycle for growth rates.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NasgroCurve(PlotMixin):
    """NASGRO 3.0 rate law for nonnegative stress ratios.

    Supply the calibrated C and n, threshold and toughness exponents p and q,
    long-crack threshold at R=0, threshold fanning constant, fixed toughness,
    Newman constraint factor and fitted maximum-to-flow stress ratio. Use
    MPa sqrt(mm) for stress intensity parameters and mm/cycle for growth rates.
    """

    coefficient: float
    exponent: float
    p: float  # pylint: disable=invalid-name
    q: float  # pylint: disable=invalid-name
    threshold_zero: float
    threshold_fanning: float
    toughness: float
    constraint: float
    peak_to_flow: float

    def get_growth_rate(
        self, length: float, k_min: float, k_max: float
    ) -> float:
        """Evaluate growth at a crack dimension and two stress intensities."""
        return nasgro_rate(astuple(self), length, k_min, k_max)

    def plot(
        self,
        length: float | None = None,
        k_min: ArrayLike = 0.0,
        k_max: ArrayLike | None = None,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        *,
        scale: _CurveScale = "semilogy",
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Plot NASGRO growth rate against maximum stress intensity.

        By default, show the long-crack reference curve at stress ratio R = 0.

        Parameters
        ----------
        length : float, optional
            Fixed crack dimension in mm for the short-crack threshold
            correction. Omit to use the long-crack limit.
        k_min : array_like, optional
            Fixed minimum intensity in MPa √mm, by default zero. With explicit
            sample arrays, supply one value or one per sample.
        k_max : array_like, optional
            Omit to sample up to the curve's toughness. A scalar sets the
            upper bound of the sweep. An array supplies exact sample points,
            each strictly below toughness. To plot one point, pass a
            one-element array.
        fig, ax : matplotlib.figure.Figure and matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            Existing figure and axes for overlays.
        scale : {"loglog", "semilogx", "semilogy"}, optional
            Axis scales, by default "semilogy". Use "semilogx" to display
            zero growth on a linear rate axis.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple of Figure and Axes
            Figure and axes containing the sampled curve.
        """
        minimum = np.asarray(k_min, dtype=float)
        maxima = np.asarray(
            self.toughness if k_max is None else k_max, dtype=float
        )
        sweep = maxima.ndim == 0
        if sweep:
            if minimum.ndim != 0:
                raise ValueError("A sweep requires a scalar k_min.")
            lower, upper = minimum.item(), maxima.item()
            if not (
                np.isfinite(upper) and 0 <= lower < upper <= self.toughness
            ):
                raise ValueError(
                    "Require 0 <= k_min < sweep upper bound <= toughness."
                )
            samples = np.linspace(lower, upper, 201)
            maxima = np.unique(
                samples[(samples > lower) & (samples < self.toughness)]
            )
        if maxima.ndim != 1 or not maxima.size:
            raise ValueError("k_max must contain at least one intensity")
        minima = np.broadcast_to(minimum, maxima.shape)
        if length is None:
            rate_at = partial(nasgro_long_crack_rate, astuple(self))
            label = "NASGRO long-crack growth rate"
        else:
            rate_at = partial(self.get_growth_rate, length)
            label = "NASGRO growth rate"
        rates = [rate_at(lower, upper) for lower, upper in zip(minima, maxima)]
        fig, ax = make_axes(fig, ax)
        _plot_curve(
            ax,
            maxima,
            rates,
            scale,
            marker="o" if maxima.size == 1 else None,
            label=label,
            nonpositive="mask",
        )
        ax.set(
            xlabel="Maximum stress intensity (MPa √mm)",
            ylabel="Growth rate (mm/cycle)",
        )
        if ax.get_yscale() == "linear":
            ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
        if sweep:
            left = lower if lower > 0 or scale == "semilogy" else None
            ax.set_xlim(left=left, right=upper)
            if upper == self.toughness:
                ax.axvline(
                    upper, color="0.4", linestyle="--", label="Toughness"
                )
        return fig, ax
